observed_response.title: Time-limited cash-floor relief with weekly collections reporting
observed_response.note: The draft proposal is an authored scenario fixture for this fictional company, shown for comparison. It was not available to either candidate run. Overlap means the same clauses were touched; it says nothing about direction or merit.

review_notes: Reviewer note on C04: the 10% figure the model cites is the memo's review criterion for assumption A2, not a contractual limit, and A08 is the model's own inferred assumption. Version 1.2 already added aged-inventory reporting; the candidate goes further and adds a limit, with no level proposed. The evidence quoted is genuine and the clause is a reasonable place for the change. The original model wording is preserved.

Reviewer note on C05: weakly supported. The disruption already met the current notice threshold (38% of volume, 24 days) and the notice was given on time, so the evidence does not show the threshold is too lax. The remaining 15.2% of delayed volume is a supply concern, not a notice failure.

Reviewer note on C06: the $45.0 million trigger worked as written; the forecast it requires was delivered on February 22, 2027. A higher trigger would give earlier visibility, which fits the scenario lender policy, but no level is proposed and the quoted forecast does not by itself show the trigger was too low.

Reviewer note on C01: the model also proposed raising the cash floor, giving the $33.6 million month-end as the reason. That change was withheld because its quotation paraphrased the cash report instead of quoting it; nothing was substituted. Its direction (tighten) is the opposite of the authored v1.3 draft, which offers time-limited relief with compensating reporting. A month-end below a floor does not show the floor is too low. The same tighten-versus-relief pattern appeared in the historical benchmark.

What this run does show: with origination evidence alone the model keeps all nine clauses; with the five reports it changes three reporting and notice clauses tied to the supply, inventory and cash assumptions and retains five. None of the three validated changes overlaps the clauses in the authored draft (C01, C03). One run of each; stability is not measured.
